judge: J1-strict-v6 (prepared-plan exception: plan sentences WITH specific research parameters can pass)
context_note: v6 was the iteration that fixed v5's over-correction (field-zeroed). v5 killed ALL plan sentences; v6 adds an exception: if a plan sentence contains specific research parameters (numbers, tool names, field names), it counts as a finding. This is the bridge between v5 (too strict) and v7+ (echo-based approaches that all failed on sham).

sham_validation.verdict: PARTIAL — sham mean 0.669 < A-full 0.810 (gap -0.141) but paired diffs are inconsistent: D1/seeda sham=A-full (both 1.0), D2/seeda sham>A-full (+0.262). Sham NOT cleanly separated at cell level.

freeze_effect.note: Freeze negative effect CONFIRMED under v6 — B-nofreeze is rank 1/9, consistent with v11/v2/v3/v4 findings. Now 5/5 judges confirm freeze effect.

conclusions: C1: v6 fixes v5's over-correction (A-full recovers to 0.810 from 0.053) but does NOT achieve clean sham separation. The prepared-plan exception lets sham's fabricated specific numbers pass.
C2: Freeze negative effect now confirmed by 5/5 judges (v11/v2/v3/v4/v6 all rank B-nofreeze 1/9 or tied lowest). Most robust finding in C3 v3 matrix.

C3: v6 is a transitional rubric — it validates the direction (plan sentences with specific params should count) but the specificity threshold is too loose. v7-v10 tried echo/freeze-trace/method-echo/instruction-dependency approaches, all failed on sham. v11's specificity-fingerprint (ratio of sentences with concrete details <0.2 → fail) is the only one that works.

C4: Six-judge panel now complete (v11/v2/v3/v4/v5/v6). Pattern: v11 is the only judge that achieves clean sham separation without side effects. v6 confirms the design trajectory was correct (v5→v6→...→v11).
